title: Joining King Oliver in St. Louis and who ran the band
summary: He joined with Red Allen and Willie Foster, going on to New York; Oliver was business-like, and Luis Russell gave the directions.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: St. Louis, Missouri. It was Red Allen, Willie Foster, and me. We joined the King Oliver Band in St. Louis. Everybody left from St. Louis to New York. He played in the Savoy Ballroom. What kind of fellow was he, Josephine?
And what did he like to do? Strictly business. Everything on a business basis, huh?

That's right. But he'd find time to laugh and joke with the men all the time. Very advised fellow, you never had much to say in the band, you only had someone else to tell the fellows what to do. Really? Yeah, he'd never tell you anything.
Who would do the telling then, I mean, when you joined the band, who would really rock the band?
Well, Louis Russell, Louis Russell did all of that.
Was he doing a range here in the band? Was he doing a range here?

Yeah, he'd do some range, he was doing a range. And we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone, but Louis Russell did all of that. After that band broke up, we went on the road. We had trombone played, they did all the business. Pete, I can't think of his name unless I look up the name.
I think I have it outside in the car. Yeah. I didn't want to get it if you wanted to.
No, it wouldn't be necessary. But anyway, he was the one to tell the fellows all what to do.
